text.p: Olivetti managing director Roberto Colaninno on Wednesday called on the Italian government to explain its plans for telecommunications market liberalisation and competition.
Speaking on the margins of the Olivetti general meeting, Colaninno criticised an agreement between Deutsche Telekom and Italian state electricity utility Enel.
Enel and Deutsche Telekom have formed a venture to compete for Italy's third mobile telephone licence. It is due to be awarded between the end of November and mid-December.
Colaninno has previously criticised the entry of Enel into the mobile telephone field. Olivetti is the majority shareholder in second mobile phone operator Omnitel.
On Wednesday, he said that the Enel-Telekom venture was "a distortion of the market and competition".

He added that if state-controlled telephone operator Telecom Italia 's plans to activate DECT advanced cordless telephone systems went ahead, the government must explain what it meant by competition and liberalisation.
Italy has not yet finalised authorisation rules for mobile phones using the Digital European Cordless Telephony standard.
The country currently has two GSM standard mobile phone service operators, state-controlled Telecom Italia Mobile (TIM) and Omnitel. Both firms are interested in DECT technology.
